_comment: Generated by tools/hooks/hooks.mjs sync in the starter: every check as shipped (core skills, packs with "pack", library skills with "skill"). Upgrades compare a project's entries with this copy (a 3-way merge), so local edits are kept. Do not edit.

requirements.message: Save the plan to docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md (plan skill) and link it in the answer, then ask the user to review it before work starts (with "autonomy": "auto", carry it out and record your choices instead).
Debug skill: state the root cause in the answer ("Root cause: <what and why>") with the evidence that shows it, found before the fix.

Debug skill: code changed for the fix, but no test did. Add a test that fails without the fix and passes with it, and run the suite. If the project has no test framework, waive it (node tools/hooks/hooks.mjs waive debug-test-added "no test framework here") and say how the fix was checked instead.
Parallel-agents skill: run the full checks on the combined result after the last change, and say in the answer what they showed, part by part.

Answers from research say where each fact comes from. Plain words are enough for a project file: "from exports/2026-W42.csv", a file opened this turn (a file you wrote this turn is not a source). Web facts get their links (numbered [1], [2] with a "Sources:" list at the end works too), each a page opened this turn. Or say plainly that nothing is recorded in the project.
Research skill: the answer says it is verified, so its ledger must pass: node skills/research/scripts/claims.mjs check .cache/research/<slug>.md, and fix every ERROR.
Skill-finder skill: report the search in the answer: "Existing skills checked: <where> - <result>".

Skill-finder skill: a third-party skill was brought in and changed. Check the wording is ours: node tools/skills.mjs compare skills/<skill> <the untouched copy> must print "0 shared run(s)". Rewrite every shared run it lists.
Plan skill: run node skills/plan/scripts/plan-tasks.mjs check <plan> and fix each warning (or give its reason) before handing the plan over.

Security-review skill: write the report table (every area PASS, FAIL or N/A with its evidence, and where each open FAIL went) to docs/reviews/security-YYYY-MM-DD.md. The answer gets one plain sentence near the end, not the table, whose words match the result and name the file: nothing failed, "The security review passed - details in docs/reviews/security-YYYY-MM-DD.md"; everything that failed is fixed, "The security review found 2 problems and I fixed both: <what> - details in ..."; something is still open, say what and where it went, never "passed" (or the short form: "Security review: 1 open - details in ..." with one "<area>: FAIL -> open (<severity>, where it went)" line each). In the user's language (Spanish: "La revisión de seguridad salió bien - detalles en ...", "FALLA -> corregido", "FALLA -> abierto").
Security-review skill: log the review in the Reviews table of docs/security.md (date, scope, result, open FAILs and where they went).

requirements.message: This turn wrote security-sensitive code (sign-in, passwords, tokens, secrets, permissions, sessions, cookies, CORS, uploads, endpoints, shell or eval, query building, deserializing, crypto, payments or personal data). Follow the security-review skill for what changed (its report table and the log line in docs/security.md), even though nobody asked. If the match is not security work, waive it: node tools/hooks/hooks.mjs waive security-code "<the specific reason, e.g. the word is a CSS class name>".

This turn changed secrets, the build pipeline or deployment settings (.env, CI workflows, Docker, hosting, infrastructure). Follow the security-review skill for those areas (Secrets, Deployment, Build pipeline, Access to infrastructure), or waive it: node tools/hooks/hooks.mjs waive security-config "<the specific reason>".

requirements.message: Something was published or deployed this turn. Hard rule 15: the security-review skill runs before anything is shared, published or released. Follow it now, log it in docs/security.md, and tell the user what it found.

A test or build failed this turn and code was changed after it: that is a fix, so the debug skill applies. Say what was wrong and why ("Root cause: <what and why>", with the evidence), found before the fix, in one or two sentences the user can follow. A test written first to fail on purpose: "Root cause: the feature did not exist yet".

Several sub-agents worked this turn: their results are only done once checked together (parallel-agents skill). Run the full checks on the combined result after the last change and say what they showed, part by part.

Fill docs/foundation.md with the user (no <...> left, status: set). In the answer, one line each for the security tests, the budget script and usability, with the result ("Security: 12 tests pass. Budget: scripts/perf_check.py PASS. Usability: plain errors, --help."); the details stay in docs/foundation.md. Plain sentences in the user's language work too (Spanish: "Seguridad: ... Rendimiento: ... Facilidad de uso: ...").

requirements.message: Code changed: add a Verification section (a heading or a bold **Verification** line) with Automated (commands and results), Real app (what was exercised on a real run, screenshot paths), Independent review (SHIP/FIX and the report path) and Still weak (docs/checks/qa-standards.md). Budgets only when the change can affect speed or size (still within docs/foundation.md, with numbers). The Finished section's "Not done or not checked" list counts as Still weak: don't repeat it. The headings may be in the language the user writes in (Spanish works). A part that doesn't apply to this change says so in one line with why.

A feature needs an independent review that ends in SHIP (fix and re-review until it does). Quote the verdict and the report path. With no person to review, start a reviewer sub-agent (the Agent or Task tool) with a read-only brief: no other reviewer is no reason to skip it.

Write or update docs/specs/<feature>.md with numbered acceptance criteria and the plan, and mark each criterion PASS or FAIL there. The answer gives one line ("Acceptance criteria: 15 of 15 PASS - docs/specs/<feature>.md"), plus one line for each criterion that failed.
Write release notes in docs/releases/ (what changed, try it fast, try it for real).
A release needs its notes in docs/releases/ and a clean attribution scan (node tools/hooks/git-guard.mjs scan) quoted in the answer.
Release runbook: decide the rollback plan before the deploy (how to undo it, and the numbers that mean roll back now), put it in the release notes, and name it in the answer.
A bugfix needs a regression test that failed before the fix and passes after it.
QA missed something the user found: report What slipped, Why QA missed it, Fix, and Process change, and add a line to docs/lessons.md.
QA runbook: report what was found. An incident gets "What slipped" and the rest of the incident report; a sweep lists its rounds, findings with evidence, fixes and what is left.
Performance work needs before and after numbers from the same tool in the answer.
Name the backup, the restore test, and the record counts before and after.

Add every foundation and app-standards security item to the review table in docs/reviews/security-YYYY-MM-DD.md, each PASS, FAIL or N/A with its evidence. The answer names that file in its one sentence about the security review (security-review skill), not the whole table.
Write the install/update test matrix into the release notes, each case marked tested or for the user to run.
Behaviour changed: raise the version number (the last part for fixes, the middle part for new features). Turned on by: node tools/packs.mjs configure app --version-file <file>.
Add a dated line to docs/CHANGELOG.md.
Bugfix: state the root cause in the answer ("Root cause: <what and why>"), found before the fix (debug skill), not a description of the symptom.

requirements.message: This turn changed a migration, a schema or the data format: follow the data-change runbook, and say how the data is backed up and restored if the change goes wrong.

requirements.message: A version was tagged or published this turn: follow the release runbook (release notes, rollback plan, attribution check).
This turn changed how the app is installed, launched or updated: follow the install-update runbook (its install matrix in docs/releases/).

Modular-code skill: keep the code easy to grow and rename. Each FAIL above names the file and line: split a file that grew past 400 lines by job, read URLs, hosts and ports from the config module (not typed in), import other modules only through their public entry. Details: skills/modular-code/SKILL.md.
Research skill, section E: record the confirmed findings in docs/knowledge (labeled, sourced, dated) so the next question is answered from the project, not re-researched.

Answer from what the project knows, and say in plain words which file each fact came from: "from docs/knowledge/x.md" or "from exports/2026-W42.csv", a file opened this turn (a note you wrote this turn is not a source; cite what it came from). Web sources are fine for what the project doesn't have. Or say plainly that the project has nothing recorded on it.
Register every ingested file in docs/knowledge/SOURCES.md (and move the originals into sources/).
Save the deliverable as a new file in outputs/ (a new version is a new file) and give its path.
Add a dated line to docs/CHANGELOG.md for the knowledge or outputs that changed.
Knowledge-capture skill: write the fact, preference or decision into docs/knowledge (labeled, sourced, dated), docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/BRIEF.md. Saying it in the answer is not recording it.
New originals arrived in sources/: follow the ingest runbook, so each one is registered in docs/knowledge/SOURCES.md and its facts are captured.
A file was written to outputs/: that is a deliverable, so follow the deliverable runbook (new version as a new file, sources, the writing check).

Facts were written into docs/knowledge: they come through the research skill (sources read this turn, cited), the knowledge-capture skill (what the user said) or the ingest runbook (a file they gave). Facts read from this project's own files pass as they are when each one has its evidence label (observed, ...), the date, and the project file it came from as its source.
Orchestrate skill: run node skills/orchestrate/scripts/ledger.mjs check <ledger> and act on everything it lists before reporting.
Backend-patterns skill: server code changed without tests. Add tests for the service logic and one success and one failure per endpoint, and run them.
Codebase-map skill: save the map to docs/codebase-map.md (with date, commit, tools used and unknowns) so later sessions reuse it.

Frontend-design skill: name the section used ("Frontend design: <letter>"). For section A, also write the design plan (direction, color, type, layout, first view, motion, the one memorable thing), say in the answer what it is, then run the gui-review-loop.

Screens changed and this project uses the frontend-design skill: check accessibility (its section E: keyboard, focus, labels, contrast, screen reader names) and say what you found in one line, in the user's language: "Accessibility: <what was checked> - PASS/FAIL" (Spanish: "Accesibilidad: <qué revisé> - correcta").
Mcp-builder skill: save the server's tools/list result and run node skills/mcp-builder/scripts/lint-tools.mjs on it until it reports no problems.
This turn wrote MCP server code: follow the mcp-builder skill, including its tool lint (node skills/mcp-builder/scripts/lint-tools.mjs).
Repo-setup skill: record in docs/STATUS.md what was set up, the baseline test results, what is missing and what is next.
Security-hardening skill: save the plan (threat model, inventory, ranked fixes) in docs/plans/ before fixing.
Commit-archaeologist skill: open the report with the bottom line and a label, Confidence: high, medium or low, and back the origin, timeline and intent with commit hashes.

Commit-archaeologist skill: back the origin, the timeline and the intent with the commit hashes they come from (short hashes are fine). If the code has no history yet, say so and waive it: node tools/hooks/hooks.mjs waive history-hashes "no commits touch it".

Compress-for-ai skill: run the protect check on every compressed file (compress-guard.mjs check <backup folder>, or protect-check.mjs <before> <after> for agent notes), fix every CHANGED line or restore the file, before reporting.
Teach skill: end each reply with one question that asks the user to take the next step, or close the session with a "Learned:" line saying what they can now do.
Architecture skill: name the file written: the docs/DECISIONS.md row (part A), the design file in docs/specs (part B), or docs/tech-debt.md (part C).

This turn added a dependency, a service or a data model change: that is an architecture decision. Record it with the architecture skill (docs/DECISIONS.md or a design spec: what, why, what it rules out, what would reopen it).
Incident-response skill: keep the incident file in docs/incidents/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md (level, timeline, impact, post-mortem) and name it in the answer.
Incident-response skill: say where the cause stands in a "Root cause: <what and why>" line, or "Root cause: not found yet" while the harm is still being stopped.

requirements.message: The user reports something down in production: follow the incident-response skill (stabilize first, timeline in docs/incidents/, root cause after).

Data-analysis skill: compute every number with code run this turn (profile.mjs, a script, or a query), and say how in a 'How it was computed:' line naming the script or query and the row count. Numbers with no output behind them are removed or marked not verified.
The answer gives numbers computed from data files: follow the data-analysis skill and show how each was computed ("How it was computed: ..." or "(calculated: ...)").
Legal-review skill: end the answer with one line saying it is not legal advice (once, at the end, never inside a letter or draft meant for someone else), and list anything that needs a lawyer.
This turn wrote a privacy policy, terms or a contract: follow the legal-review skill and say plainly that it is not legal advice.
Marketing skill: name the brand voice used, and give every statistic, result, benchmark and competitor fact its source, or leave a visible placeholder ([stat needed: <what>, source?]).
User-research skill: give every theme its count as "n of N" with quotes traced to participant IDs, or, for a study plan, name the decision it informs.

require.answerMatches: \bnot (been |yet )?sent\b|\bnothing (was|has been) sent\b|\bno se ha enviado\b|\bno (lo |la )?(he|hemos) enviado\b|\bsin enviar\b

requirements.message: Correspondence skill: save the draft as a new file in outputs/drafts/ (YYYY-MM-DD-<recipient>-<topic>.md), show it in the answer, and say plainly that it was not sent, with what the user must check before sending (placeholders, worked-out figures, tone).

Data-pipeline skill: pipeline inputs changed. Check each new or changed input against its schema before any step uses it: node skills/data-pipeline/scripts/schema-check.mjs <input> <schema.json>. A FAIL stops the run: fix the source or record the schema change (section C).

Dependency-update skill: a manifest or lockfile changed. Run the same gates as before the change (tests, build, lint, type check) and compare them in the answer, one line per gate: "Before/after: tests 214 pass -> 214 pass". A gate that passed before and fails now means roll back (section G).

Game-dev skill: scenes or scripts changed, so build, test, export and start the game before reporting: node skills/game-dev/scripts/export-smoke.mjs --preset "<preset>" --out builds/<target>/<Game>.<ext> (or the engine tests: GUT, GdUnit4, dotnet test, Unity -runTests).

Manuscript skill: run node skills/manuscript/scripts/continuity.mjs on the chapters (with --style for the style sheet), or end the answer with a line "Continuity: <what was checked and found>" ("Continuity: not checked this turn (summaries only)" when nothing was).

ML-experiments skill: a model was trained or scored this turn, so log the run: node skills/ml-experiments/scripts/exp-log.mjs add experiments/log.md --name <run> --data <data> --params "<k=v>" --seed <n> --score "<metric>=<value>+-<spread>".

Mobile-app skill: app code changed, so run the platform's checks before reporting: flutter analyze and flutter test, ./gradlew lint testDebugUnitTest, xcodebuild test, or npx tsc --noEmit / npx eslint . / npx jest.

Notes-vault skill: notes changed, so run the link check: node skills/obsidian/scripts/notes.mjs check --all (note folders outside docs/ are read only with --all). Fix every broken link this turn caused and report the ones that were already there.

Package-release skill: preview the package before it goes out. Run its dry run this turn (npm pack --dry-run, cargo package --list, python -m build then twine check dist/*, dart pub publish --dry-run, dotnet pack, gem build) and read the file list: no secrets, no private fixtures, license and entry points present.

Routines skill: docs/routines.md changed, so validate it: node skills/routines/scripts/routines.mjs check must print RESULT: PASS (a known Every, an existing runbook, Last run as YYYY-MM-DD or never). Fix every problem it lists.

Web-app-patterns skill: client code changed, so prove it: run the component tests (npx vitest run, npx jest, npm test) or the type check (npx tsc --noEmit, npx vue-tsc --noEmit, npx svelte-check), and before a build ships run node skills/web-app-patterns/scripts/client-secrets.mjs . and fix every FAIL.
